summaries.demographer: Randy Dodd is a five-year-old White, non-Hispanic boy living with both parents in Quitman, Louisiana, and he has never been married or partnered (Q84, Q88-Q89, Q98-Q99). He is enrolled in kindergarten, has less than a ninth-grade education, and is not in the workforce (Q90-Q92, Q65-Q75). His household appears stable and parent-led, with no temporary members, lodgers, or absent household members (Q11-Q14, Q51-Q55). His social life is age-graded around parents, grandparents, cousins, classmates, church, and peewee soccer (Q05-Q07, Q47).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Randy's choices are driven by curiosity, immediate sensory rewards, and adult-bounded routines: he wants candy, toys, tablet time, and LEGO sets, but parents impose waiting, limits, and safety rules (Q32, Q48, Q60-Q62). He shows early problem-solving persistence, choosing to open a broken toy car with help instead of discarding it and documenting what he finds (Q02-Q03). His time preferences are childlike but trainable: he wants to spend or continue activities immediately, while adults teach delayed gratification around toys, money, and screen time (Q48, Q61-Q62). Uncertainty is managed through trusted adults, predictable routines, and concrete reassurance from parents and teachers (Q42, Q44, Q50).
summaries.political_scientist: Randy is below voting age and has no partisan identification, explicitly saying he is neither Democrat nor Republican and does not understand parties (Q23-Q24, Q95-Q96). His civic orientation is developmental rather than ideological: he values fairness as turn-taking, kindness, helping neighbors, and public helpers such as firefighters and police at parades (Q20-Q24, Q65, Q109). Institutional trust is mediated through family, school, church, doctors, and visible local helpers (Q42, Q47, Q95). Race and policing issues are only minimally understood; he frames them through classroom norms of treating everyone kindly (Q26-Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Randy presents as curious, calm, resilient, and practically oriented, especially in toy experiments, LEGO building, puzzles, and trying again after soccer mistakes (Q01-Q03, Q43, Q65). His emotional regulation is age-appropriate: he experiences frustration, separation worry, fear of thunder and shots, and disappointment, but uses hugs, breathing, building, drawing, teacher reassurance, and parental support to calm down (Q38-Q45, Q50). His self-concept centers on being a 'fixing boy,' a future firefighter or engineer, and a member of family, class, church, and soccer team (Q02, Q65, Q95, Q108). Attachment figures are strong and concrete, especially mother, father, teacher, grandmother, and church community (Q05-Q07, Q47, Q49).
